content.value_statement: Misleading media often pairs authentic pixels with false captions, while detector scores create false certainty. This skill prioritizes provenance, physical consistency, and transparent limits.
actual_capabilities: Defines a provenance-first workflow for authenticating images and videos.
Separates caption accuracy, origin, manipulation, synthesis, location, and date into distinct findings.
Guides metadata, C2PA, lighting, shadow, reflection, geometry, compression, and noise checks.
Explains durable AI-generation indicators and the limits of automated detectors.
Adapts tests to originals, platform re-encodes, screenshots, and other processed copies.
Produces evidence-based conclusions with assumptions, invalid tests, and open questions.
limitations: It cannot prove authenticity when only a heavily processed copy is available.
It does not replace specialist laboratory analysis, legal process, or access to original devices.
Detector scores, metadata, and missing search results cannot support conclusions alone.
Some checks require external tools, archives, search engines, or corroborating records.

use_cases.title: Verify Breaking News Media
use_cases.description: Trace earlier copies, compare captions, and test claimed locations before publishing or sharing.

use_cases.title: Review Submitted Evidence
use_cases.description: Assess provenance, processing history, and manipulation indicators in claims, onboarding, or evidence review.

use_cases.title: Investigate Synthetic Media
use_cases.description: Evaluate physical consistency, structural coherence, metadata, and detector limitations without relying on one score.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Media Claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [media] against this claim: [claim]. Start with provenance, identify the best copy, and report evidence, uncertainty, and invalid tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one image or video claim

prompt_templates.title: Trace Earlier Publication
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify whether [media] appeared earlier under another caption. Compare source dates, credits, archived pages, keyframes, and location clues.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Manipulation
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [file] for manipulation or synthesis. Classify its processing history, then assess metadata, geometry, lighting, compression, and durable structural indicators.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed forensic assessment of a supplied file

prompt_templates.title: Test Competing Hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [media] under authentic, recontextualized, manipulated, and synthetic hypotheses. Rank evidence, test alternatives, document assumptions, and define decisive follow-up evidence.

output_examples.input: A social post says this explosion video was recorded today in City A.
output: An archived news page published the same skyline footage eighteen months earlier in another country.
The available copy is a platform re-encode, so signal-level authenticity tests are invalid.
Audio may be edited because a hard cut aligns with a noise-floor change.

output_examples.input: Determine whether this portrait is AI-generated.
output: No reliable provenance was found, but absence of provenance does not prove synthesis.
Lighting and perspective remain coherent, while small background text shows localized structural errors.
Obtain the original file and compare multiple independent indicators before reaching a stronger conclusion.

output_examples.input: Check whether this screenshot proves the quoted account posted the message.
output: Conclusion: the screenshot alone cannot verify authorship.
Interface layout is plausible, but screenshots can be recreated without image-editing traces.
Verify the underlying post, archived captures, account history, and platform identifiers.

best_practices: State the exact claim before testing and separate each conclusion by origin, caption, location, date, manipulation, and synthesis.
Obtain the least processed copy, record its source and history, hash it, and work on duplicates.
Document negative results, invalid tests, assumptions, and evidence that could change the conclusion.
anti_patterns: Do not label media fake from one detector score, heatmap, metadata field, or visual anomaly.
Do not run signal-level tests on screenshots or platform re-encodes without explaining why results are unreliable.
Do not upload sensitive, intimate, victim, or confidential media to services that retain or publish submissions.

faq.question: Can this skill prove a photo is real?
faq.answer: It can verify specific claims and evidence. It cannot prove every unseen aspect of authenticity.

faq.question: Does missing metadata mean an image is fake?
faq.answer: No. Platforms and editing workflows often remove metadata, so absence is usually inconclusive.

faq.question: Are AI-image detector scores reliable?
faq.answer: They are weak signals with false positives and false negatives. Never use one score as the conclusion.

faq.question: Why does the workflow start with provenance?
faq.answer: Earlier copies and original captions often resolve false claims faster and more defensibly than pixel analysis.

faq.question: Can it analyze video?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers keyframes, containers, encoders, frame behavior, audio consistency, provenance, and processing loss.

faq.question: What is needed for the strongest assessment?
faq.answer: Provide the best available file, exact claim, source context, known processing history, and any original publication links.
